title: A class zero in filtered complex homology vanishes at a later stage
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and D a diagram of cochain complexes of A-modules indexed by the natural numbers with their usual order. For an integer n, a stage e, and a class x in H^n(D_e), suppose the homology map induced by the canonical cocone leg D_e to colim D sends x to zero. Then there is b at least e such that the homology map of D(e to b) sends x to zero. Cochain complexes and homology are as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].

source.place: Lemma 10.8.8, Tag 00DB, homology of directed colimits; also used in Tag 08DD

proof.text: ModuleCat.AB gives exactness of filtered colimits. Shrink AB5 to the size of the natural-number indexing category. Regard a diagram of short complexes as a short complex of diagrams. Evaluation preserves homology, so its homology is naturally the pointwise homology diagram. The exact colimit functor preserves homology as well. Compose the two homology isomorphisms; homologyMap_mapNatTrans applied to each cocone leg verifies the resulting colimit cocone.

The adjacent-short-complex functor preserves colimits because all three evaluation functors do. Transport preservation across homologyFunctorIso to get preservation of colimits by degree-n complex homology.

The forgetful functor on modules preserves the filtered colimit. Apply Concrete.isColimit_exists_of_rep_eq to the equality of the image of x and the image of zero. This gives a common stage b and arrows e to b. Those arrows coincide because the indexing category is a preorder. Their maps preserve zero, giving the conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem filteredModuleComplex_homology_eventually_zero
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (D : ℕ ⥤ CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (n : ℤ) (e : ℕ) (x : (D.obj e).homology n)
    (hx : HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (colimit.ι D e) n x = 0) :
    ∃ (b : ℕ) (h : e ≤ b),
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (D.map (homOfLE h)) n x = 0
